---
title: Prepare your data
---

Choose the route that matches your question before changing the input table.

| What you have | Route | Required inputs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expression and clinical data | Pathway-first | Expression, clinical table and gene sets |
| Named genes, signatures or scores | Exposure-first | Feature table and explicit feature names |
| A saved RDS, workbook or delivery folder | Read or plot | The saved result and the requested task |

## Expression and clinical data

Use a numeric expression matrix with genes in rows and samples in columns,
unless you explicitly set another orientation. The clinical table has one row
per analysis subject and a unique sample ID column. Match IDs explicitly;
column position alone is not a sample map.

Keep the original expression scale and any transformation recorded. TPM,
log-transformed abundance and standardized scores are different inputs. Gene
identifiers must match the gene sets; inspect coverage before interpreting scores.
Bundled IOBR signatures, supported curated sets and user-supplied membership
are described in the [pathway-first chapter](workflows/pathway-first.qmd).

## A feature table

Each row is one subject. Keep identifiers, features, endpoints and baseline
covariates in separate named columns. For example:

| ID | Selected_score | Age | Sex | Response | OS_time | OS_status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S001 | 0.42 | 61 | F | 1 | 12.5 | 1 |
| S002 | -0.15 | 68 | M | 0 | 20.0 | 0 |

These two rows illustrate the format only. They cannot support a fitted analysis.
Name the requested features explicitly so unrelated numeric columns stay out.

## Define endpoints and covariates

- **Response:** record exactly what 1 and 0 mean, including how CR/PR and other
  categories are handled. Missing response is not automatically non-response.
- **OS:** provide time, event status, the event code and time unit. Check event
  and censoring counts after matching subjects.
- **Covariates:** use the agreed baseline adjustment set. A tutorial list such
  as Age, Sex and ECOG is an example, not a verified set for every study.

Check duplicate IDs, missing values, invalid categories and unsupported exposure
contrasts before execution. Keep the full requested feature family for FDR;
selecting a display subset does not redefine that family.
